title: Training Regimen of an Elite Ultramarathon Runner: A Case Study of What Led Up to the 24-Hour World-Record Run
authors: Byrne J, Lynch S, Mokha GM
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: One elite male ultramarathoner (8 world records in 2021-2022, including 319.6 km in 24 h); Strava/Coros data Dec 2020 to Sept 2022
findings: Five training blocks, with volume per block averaging 172.1 to 263 km/week and a maximum of 378 km/week.
Peak running volume per block occurred on average 3.2 weeks before races.
The week after a race was a recovery week with 19 km running and more cross-training.
Interval-type workouts (1-10 km repeats) were completed throughout the blocks; the 24-h average pace (4:30/km) closely matched the overall average training pace.
limitations: Single elite athlete (n = 1), descriptive only, no controls; volumes are far beyond what a recreational athlete could safely use.
implications: Use only the structure, not the volumes: peak volume about 3 weeks before the goal race, a very short post-race recovery week (19 km, roughly 7-11% of the athlete's block averages by simple arithmetic), and quality work retained through blocks.
Do not scale the 172-378 km/week figures to recreational plans; cap volume by the athlete's own history and injury risk.

verification.notes: Crossref (2024-04-01) and Europe PMC abstract re-fetched; numbers confirmed. The percentage of a typical week is the verifier's arithmetic (19/263 to 19/172).
